reason: I run three-plus AI agents every day and lose context every time I switch between them, so a shared session, skill, and credential layer is exactly the pain I have. With the first five humans free it costs me nothing to try, and $30/seat/month is trivial once my team passes five.
objection: It's one local daemon from a single developer — if loomd goes down, every agent stops, and I can't force my team onto a new tool I don't trust to be maintained.
would_change_my_mind: If Claude Code and Cursor had native, battle-tested Loom plugins instead of a new daemon I install and run myself.
